newsitem.title: USA: New Norfolk Southern move in Conrail fight.
newsitem.headline: New Norfolk Southern move in Conrail fight.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp. said Monday it will seek to replace most of Conrail Inc.'s board of directors as part of its four-month effort to take control of the East Coast railroad giant.

Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern nominated a slate of five directors to serve on the Conrail board and will seek to maintain three current board members as part of its plan to reduce the board size to eight from 13.
Norfolk Southern unveiled the plan on the last day that it would be permitted to submit a board slate for Conrail's Dec. 19 annual shareholders meeting.
Norfolk Southern is trying to derail a proposed friendly merger between Conrail and Richmond, Va.-based CSX Corp.
Norfolk Southern is bidding $10.3 billion in cash for Philadelphia-based Conrail, whose cash-and-stock merger with CSX is valued at about $9.5 billion.
Conrail said that Norfolk Southern's proposals to gain control of Conrail's board appeared to be illegal under U.S. transportation laws.
Also, Conrail said Norfolk Southern's proposals to remove Conrail's incumbent directors and to reduce the number of board members were invalid under Pennsylvania law.

Conrail announced last week that it had scheduled its annual meeting, normally held in May, for Dec. 19, and that in the meantime it would work to winning approval of the deal from shareholders and federal regulators. Last month, shareholder rejected a key provision that would have allowed the deal to go ahead.
The chiefs of all three railroads met Jan. 31, but would not say what was discussed and pledged to keep quiet about future talks.
